# Let's catch up

Welcome to Issue 043.

I'm back after a bit of a hiatus.
Life's been busy, so I haven't had much time to write.
I usually commit myself to an hour a day, but the time just hasn't been there recently.
So, I'm recommiting myself to drafting these updates, with some modifications.

Let's get back to it.

# Three things

Here's what caught my attention this week:

### [Now Entering the Era of Bleh](https://www.noemamag.com/now-entering-the-era-of-bleh/) (article)

This piece shares some arguments on the impact AI will have on knowledge work.
The author's statements about homogenization of output and product development caught my attention.
An interesting point was raised: if everyone has the same tools, then there's no more competitive advantage.

### [GEO is a distraction](https://www.mariehaynes.com/geo-is-a-distraction/) (blog)

This blog post brings into question the effectiveness of AI to direct traffic to websites.
According to data used in the post, traffic from all LLMs only accounted for only 0.73% of referrels.
The story was the same for conversions, where Google organic accounted for over 96% of total conversions.
This quote from the post sums it all up:

> The AI search that is actually sending people to businesses today isn't ChatGPT.
> It's Google.

### [How CNN Is Applying Data and AI In The News Media Business](https://www.forbes.com/sites/randybean/2026/09/28/how-cnn-is-applying-data-and-ai-in-the-news-media-business/?) (article)

This piece highlights CNN's views on the role data and AI plays within their operations.
In short, the aim is that all decisions are data informed.
A mandate on how to do this was shared in the article, and it's worth a review.
CNN places a heavy emphasis on being able to quickly test new ideas and features, many of which are evaluated through the use of A/B testing.
There was also some discussion about focusing on further developing a semantic layer for the network's data.

Check out the links above for the full story in each item.

# What I found interesting this week

I'm once again reconfiguring these updates.
The majority of my overall writing time has been focused on these updates.
Much of this effort went into reading, summarizing, and reflecting on why each source matters in terms of what I've been learning about the media industry.
A good chunk of time was devoted to finding relevant material to include in each issue.
I've come to notice that this limits my ability to blog in other areas I find interesting, like data science, analytics, and tech.
I miss writing about those topics.
I've also come to notice the overhead of how I currently do this just wasn't paying off, and it resulted in me missing my self-imposed weekly deadline from time-to-time.

So, I'm adding some constraints and making some modifications.
The sections will remain the same, but when it comes to the weekly items that caught my attention, I'm only going to add a sentence or two of summary along with a sentence or two about why it matters.
Other than that, much of the rest of this update will remain the same.
